chapter: Los Angeles scene and the Ellington sound
title: First noticing race restrictions in Los Angeles
summary: He ran with anyone growing up, then saw race-restriction signs on new house tracts near Crenshaw.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Because you were saying that you pretty much did whatever you wanted to do, wherever you wanted to.
Sure. I ran around with anybody I wanted.
Not to be running around, I was just in the school, and everything else, so --
WILLARD without any awareness of any
When were you first aware of it in Southern California?

When I saw signs on these tracts, house tracts, where they used to have streets and streets of these little cottages, and along maybe they'd say something about race restrictions, and I said huh, what is this?
In what part of town was that?

Usually out around what is now the Crenshaw area, and west. See, they were -- I remember when they were around 12th Avenue, and Jefferson and Adams, along there, they were building these tracts of small homes, see.
